Concept: THE HELPFUL KNOCK. An unusually intimate, diagonal tabletop composition, seen at table height with a slight elevated angle and wide perspective. The fluffy cat reclines across the far half of an emerald-green trading table, head in upper right looking knowingly at the viewer, one large white forepaw stretching diagonally toward the near lower left edge. Show the decisive instant as his paw tips ONE ominous red-and-black illustrated calamity card over the edge toward the viewer. The card has a simple pictorial lightning-struck tower with no writing, and is visibly falling into the foreground; its movement reads clearly. Around the extreme left and right edges, only parts of two traders' warm expressive hands and jacket sleeves enter the picture, one pausing above a small stack of gold coins, the other holding a few cards. They are secondary, cropped supporting storytelling. The cat's bushy tail curls up behind him making an arch, his brilliant green eyes are a second focal point after the paw. Dramatic foreshortening, large shapes, asymmetric composition, cat about 60% of the image. Warm amber late-afternoon light in an old stucco courtyard trading house, background simplified deep indigo and terracotta. Emerald felt, gold coins, black-red falling card. Wry humor, protective agency, story immediately legible; never a generic seated cat portrait. Anatomically coherent cat with four legs total, only naturally visible paws. No mystical beams or floating decorative clutter.

Concept: THE CROSSING. A daring low viewpoint along a narrow bridge made from chunky alternating emerald-green and vermilion-red financial candlestick columns over a dark indigo ravine. The bridge recedes on a strong lower-left to upper-right diagonal into a sunlit Mexican-inspired market archway with simple terracotta and turquoise architecture. The cat has just walked toward the viewer and pauses in the foreground on a broad green column; his body in three-quarter view, one forepaw lifted midstep, his head twisted back over his shoulder to check on THREE much smaller adult trader travelers cautiously following him from the distance. The travelers wear simplified ordinary dark waistcoats and jackets and carry small satchels, no readable logos. He dominates 60% of the artwork, his face, luminous eyes, white ruff and fluffy orange-brown body beautifully clear. His huge tail sweeps in a bold S-curve back through the composition, visually connecting him with his followers. A few subtle gold glints on the safe footholds, sunlight crossing the scene. Bridge geometrically plausible, narrow but readable with solid connected foot surfaces; candle wicks secondary design detail. Convey careful, trusted guidance rather than falling or peril, no terror. Bold angular planes, vivid color, very strong silhouette and depth. No chart overlays, no screens, no grids, no decorative floating coins. This is a warm loteria allegory for trading with a guide.

Concept: THE SECRET ROUTE. A surprising almost straight-down view of an old ochre parchment trading map spread across a dark teal wooden table. The cat sprawls diagonally from upper left to lower right across the map with his fluffy white chest and front paws toward lower right; he tilts his head upward to meet the viewer's gaze with brilliant chartreuse eyes. His enormous bushy brown-orange tail curves around to make a graceful open spiral in the upper and left side of the scene. Map routes and terrain transform subtly into a small dimensional physical landscape: very low angular terracotta market buildings, winding indigo hazardous ravines, simple branching gold routes. THREE tiny adult trader travelers in simple coats with satchels walk in single file along the ONE luminous gold path revealed by the inner curve of his tail, heading toward a small sunlit market gate in upper right. The cat remains a naturally proportioned animal at tabletop scale; the traders and landscape are miniature map-scale allegorical figures, intentionally fantastical. His body comfortably blocks the dark dangerous branching paths while his tail defines the safe way through. The visual surprise should be a lounging cat who is also the guardian of a tiny world, not a generic cat sitting beside a map. Cat covers roughly 60% of the picture, face in lower-right third, body and tail form a diagonal and open circular frame. Strong large shapes, restrained small map details, no labels or text, no compass lettering, no extra props. Amber and ochre paper, deep teal shadows, rust-brown fur and creamy ruff, bright gold path. Rich warm directional light, playful wisdom, vibrant faceted rendering matched to reference deck.
